run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T12:34:41Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by failed POST /api/checkout traffic: frontend-proxy's 'ingress' spans carry http.status_code 504 with ~15 s durations and its 'router frontend egress' spans carry error="true"/http.status_code=0, while the Envoy access log on frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-jft59 shows 'POST /api/checkout ... 504 UT response_timeout' at exactly 15000 ms and 200 via_upstream for the other routes. The checkout service is the source of those timeouts: its own error spans are HTTP POST client spans taking ~30.0 s that end with otel.status_description 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout'; 100.67.49.77:8080 is the ClusterIP/port of the email service, and checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans take ~30.2 s. A Chaos Mesh Schedule named otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition spawned a new NetworkChaos at 12:34:31 and then every minute through 12:41:31, each 'Applied' to otel-demo/email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w, otel-demo/email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn and otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs and recovered ~55 s later ('Time up according to the duration'), so a network partition between the email pods and the checkout pod is the deepest observed cause: checkout→email TCP connects time out at 30 s, which exceeds the proxy's 15 s route timeout, so the proxy answers 504 and its error-rate alert fires. All 22 pods were Running/Ready with 0 restarts and the email Service had both pod IPs as endpoints with a matching selector, so pod crash, OOM, missing endpoints or selector mismatch are excluded. Frontend itself recorded no ERROR-status spans (its error series exists and is 0 all window) and its other routes kept returning 200, so the fault is not a frontend-wide failure; email's own spans carry http.status_code 200 but its request rate roughly halved (send_order_confirmation 5 m rate ~0.67/s before 12:34 → 0.29-0.35/s after), consistent with part of its inbound connects being dropped.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's span metrics in the window contain only two operations, 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress', with status codes STATUS_CODE_ERROR, STATUS_CODE_OK and STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

frontend-proxy 'ingress' ERROR-status span rate was 0 or ~0.0037/s until 12:34, then rose to 0.085/s at 12:36:41, 0.20/s at 12:37:41, peaked at 0.367/s at 12:40:41 and was still 0.29-0.34/s between 12:41 and 12:46; the service-level ERROR span rate follows the same shape (0.008/s before, 0.20-0.35/s from 12:37).

The sampled frontend-proxy error spans are all operation 'ingress' with status tags error=true, http.status_code="504", otel.status_code="ERROR" and durations of ~15,000,000-15,001,496 µs (15 s), e.g. span 317f5eeff095f1f6 in trace 9d48a9b96ce8529d9cc951391a1769cd and the twelve rows of the 12:42:46-12:43:23 slice.

frontend-proxy's 'router frontend egress' spans (the proxy's upstream call to the frontend service) carry status tags error="true" and http.status_code="0", i.e. the upstream call itself failed; one such sample is span be4637feabb8a3eb with duration 15,001,318 µs.

frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-jft59's Envoy access log between 12:41:32 and 12:42:14 records 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout' with response duration 14999-15002 ms against upstream frontend 100.64.242.158:8080, while in the same minutes 'GET /api/products/...' , 'POST /api/cart' and 'GET /api/data' returned 200 via_upstream.

checkout's own error spans are 'HTTP POST' client spans with error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR, duration ~30,001,176 µs and otel.status_description 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout'; their parents are oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans of ~30.0-30.3 s (e.g. traces a57417e20af37b3fa61f51b34ad82272, fd3b3a6abf90ea2ee259b89ba31b9984, 0d4ec23a3aaf8c0c3e0dcda77e52a6f3 started ~12:39:52-12:39:53).

The address in that error, 100.67.49.77:8080, is the ClusterIP and port of the otel-demo 'email' Service (selector opentelemetry.io/name=email, ports tcp-service 8080→8080), i.e. the failing checkout call is a call to the email service.

checkout's ERROR-status span rate was 0 before 12:34 and 0.063-0.187/s from 12:37 to 12:46 (time series starting only at ~12:37), i.e. checkout is the second service with a real error burst in this window; accounting, frontend and payment report 0 for the whole window and ad/fraud-detection/recommendation show only the same ~0.0037/s blips seen before the incident.

A Chaos Mesh Schedule named otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition spawned NetworkChaos objects otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-jdmmj (12:34:31), -hddgv (12:35:31), -mznpj (12:36:31), -zl9p2 (12:37:31), -7rvkf (12:38:31), -8p7rs (12:39:31), -4f5lv (12:40:31) and -5c2dr (12:41:31); each event set contains 'Experiment has started', 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn', '... email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w', '... checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs', and ~55 s later 'Time up according to the duration' plus 'Successfully recover chaos' for the same three pods.

PodNetworkChaos events exist for exactly three pods in otel-demo — checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs, email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w and email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn — with the earliest returned timestamps at 12:34:31Z, repeating each minute up to 12:41:31.

The email service still produces spans (http.status_code 200 on POST /send_order_confirmation) but at a lower rate: the 5 m rate of send_order_confirmation was ~0.43-0.67/s before 12:34 and 0.29-0.35/s from 12:36 to 12:46, and the 1 m rate fell from ~1.0-1.7/s bursts before 12:34 to ~0.5-0.73/s afterwards.

The frontend service recorded no ERROR-status spans across the window (its ERROR-rate series is present and 0 at every step), yet its POST /api/checkout server span in the failing trace lasted 15,000,276 µs with http.status_code=200, and its span rates for GET /, /api/cart, /api/data, /api/products, /api/recommendations stayed non-zero until ~12:47.

All 22 pods in otel-demo are listed Running and Ready with restart counts of 0, no waiting reason and no last termination reason, including frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-jft59, frontend-675fd7b5c5-kzdpp, checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs and both email pods (email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w, email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn).

The email Service's Endpoints object contains both email pod IPs (100.96.2.7 for email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn and 100.96.3.218 for email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w) on port 8080, and those pods carry the label opentelemetry.io/name=email that the Service selects, so service-to-pod wiring was intact.

Root cause chain: the recurring network partition applied to both email pods and the checkout pod (Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition, first NetworkChaos started 12:34:31, ~55 s per spawn every 60 s) dropped checkout→email packets, so checkout's HTTP POST to the email ClusterIP 100.67.49.77:8080 failed after a 30 s TCP dial timeout, PlaceOrder blocked ~30 s, POST /api/checkout exceeded frontend-proxy's 15 s route timeout, and frontend-proxy answered 504 ('UT response_timeout'), driving its RequestErrorRate above 0. Confirmation would be reading the NetworkChaos/Schedule spec (direction, loss/partition mode, percent of pods) which the permitted Kubernetes kinds do not expose.

Pod crash, OOM or restart of frontend-proxy, frontend or email did not cause the errors: every listed pod in otel-demo is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, and no pod shows a waiting reason or a last termination reason such as OOMKilled or Failed.

A missing endpoint or Service selector mismatch on the email Service was considered and rejected: the Endpoints object lists both email pod IPs on port 8080 and the Service selector opentelemetry.io/name=email matches the email pods' labels.

An application-level failure of the email service (5xx or error spans) was considered and rejected for the observed window: email's spans are POST /send_order_confirmation and send_email with http.status_code 200 and no error status tags; what changed is that fewer connections reached it, not that it answered errors.

Against a frontend-wide failure: in the failing trace and in the proxy access log the non-checkout routes (GET /api/products/..., POST /api/cart, GET /api/data) returned 200 via_upstream with millisecond durations in the same minutes that POST /api/checkout returned 504, and the frontend ERROR-span series is 0 throughout; only the checkout path that waits on checkout→email was affected.

Against other checkout dependencies being the failing hop: in the complete trace examined at 12:43:01 the checkout calls to CartService/GetCart, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, CurrencyService/Convert, PaymentService/Charge, shipping /get-quote, /ship-order and CartService/EmptyCart all returned success status (rpc.grpc.status_code 0 or unset with 200 ms-class durations); only the email dial produced an ERROR span.

gaps: The alerting rule could not be retrieved: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned status no_data (view d59a78df-fab2-4260-b9ba-428cf8e9635f-t2), so the exact expression, threshold and the reported value 0.2444 could not be reproduced from metrics.

The email Deployment object query (readyReplicas, container readiness/liveness probe configuration) was not delivered as citable evidence in this Run, so the Deployment status and probe settings could not be reported as facts; only pod-level containerStatuses were verified.

The NetworkChaos/Schedule custom resources are not among the readable Kubernetes kinds; only their Events were visible, so the partition's direction, loss/percent, selected pod mode and the schedule's owner/intent could not be read, and change_history is not integrated to show who created or edited the experiment.

Email container logs returned no data for email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w and email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn (status no_data on views 56d0898e-dad1-470c-bfb9-d517663a6409-t1 and 25e38bf9-af6c-4274-9f1d-15b8f3b5495b-t0; current stream read 0 bytes, previous instance not found), so email-side application behavior could not be confirmed from logs.

kube-state-metrics Deployment series for email/checkout/frontend/frontend-proxy returned no data (status no_data, view 25e38bf9-af6c-4274-9f1d-15b8f3b5495b-t1), so deployment readiness is unknown from metrics.

Trace metrics carry no pod label, so which of the two email pods lost checkout traffic (or whether both did) cannot be determined; the email pods sit on different nodes (i-071e7666000f6d243 vs i-0ba95c8c42c78df23).
The checkout error slice and the frontend-proxy error search were truncated (139 of 147 and 655 of 667 rows omitted), so the full span population behind the aggregates was not inspected.

cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping, quote, kafka, image-provider, load-generator and flagd have no ERROR-status span series in this window, which is unknown rather than zero; only the one fully fetched trace and the sampled spans show them returning success.

The sporadic single frontend-proxy errors present before 12:34 (about 0.0037/s) and the one 503 sample at 12:33:28 (GET /api/recommendations via load-generator) are not explained by the 12:34:31 chaos spawn and were not investigated further.
next_steps: Read the Schedule/NetworkChaos spec for otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition (chaos-mesh CRs) to confirm direction, loss/partition mode and selected pod percentage, and decide whether this recurring experiment on the email/checkout link is intended for the environment.
If the partition is not intended, suspend the Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition and re-check frontend-proxy ingress ERROR rate and checkout 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080' spans.

Align timeout budgets: checkout's email HTTP call allowed ~30 s while frontend-proxy's route timeout is 15 s, so every email stall becomes a user-visible 504; shorten the email client timeout and/or add a readiness probe to the email container so a degraded pod is removed from Endpoints.
Add per-pod attribution (k8s.pod.name / pod label in trace metrics) so future partitions can be tied to a specific email replica.
